description:
Raccoons don't really wash their food — scientists call it dousing. Captive raccoons dunk clean and dirty food equally, so cleaning was never the point.
Why do raccoons dip food in water? Wetting food supercharges their sense of touch: raccoon forepaws carry 4–5x more touch receptors than most mammals, and two-thirds of their sensory brain is wired to those paws.
